scene_notes: The protest–window‑breaking scene with a baseball bat is coherent, imageable, and has a clear violent‑protester prototype. The main issues are misplacement of the protest organizer and journalist along the plausibility scale, not with the underlying event structure.

The bakery–bread–serrated knife scene is well-formed, prototypical, and easily photographed, and it can support all four plausibility levels with better-chosen mid-level agents; current misplacement of butcher and chef is an agent-selection issue, not a scene problem.

The scene of digging a trench with a shovel on a construction site is clear, has a strong prototype (construction worker), and is easily photographable. The thematic gradient fails only because the gardener is placed too low in plausibility; with a better-chosen related-but-wrong construction role, the full gradient would be well supported.

This is a strong, well-specified artistic scene with an appropriate instrument and a clear prototypical agent, and it supports a full conceptual plausibility gradient; the main weakness lies not in the scene but in the visual similarity of the chosen art-related professions.

Eating pizza at a pizzeria is an everyday activity open to virtually all professions, so all four agents are perceived as plausible diners and the intended plausibility gradient cannot be realized, even though the instrument and location are appropriate and imageable.

The classroom whiteboard context has a clear prototypical agent (teacher) and can support a full plausibility gradient with better-chosen agents, but the instrument 'dry-erase marker' is not the usual tool for erasing a whiteboard drawing, so the scene needs redesign (e.g., changing the instrument to an eraser or cloth) in addition to fixing agent choices.

This is a strong, well-defined medical scene with an appropriate instrument and a clear prototypical agent (nurse), and it is easily imageable. The gradient currently collapses at the top because the medical intern is too plausible, but suitable alternative agents exist to restore a clean plausibility gradient.

The action 'opening a gift box with a letter opener at a holiday party' is too generic and socially broad: many different professions or roles can plausibly perform it, and there is no clear professional prototype for the event. This makes it impossible to construct robust implausible-hard and implausible-easy conditions with human agents, so the scene itself does not support the required plausibility gradient.

The scene 'painting a wooden door with a brush in a workshop' is coherent, uses an appropriate instrument, and has a clear prototypical profession (painter/decorator or carpenter). The main issue is the choice of implausible_hard agent and the visual similarity among the three trades, not the underlying scene, which can support the intended gradient with better-selected agents.

The action of scooping ice cream with a metal spoon at a dessert buffet is clear, physically appropriate, and strongly tied to front-of-house food service, providing a solid prototype (waiter) and a meaningful gradient with related but less fitting roles. The scene is easy to depict in a single image, and any minor visual issues pertain to agent choice rather than the underlying event structure.

The shotgun–clay pigeon–shooting range configuration is prototypical and easily photographed. The domain is well-defined and leaves room for related-but-wrong professionals to occupy the implausible_hard slot if the marksman is replaced.

The kitchen/batter/wooden spoon/copper pot scene is clear, prototypically culinary, and easy to depict, with a strong prototype (chef). The main issue is that ‘pastry chef’ is as prototypical as ‘chef’, collapsing the top two tiers; with alternative agents, the gradient would be well supported.

The emergency-room touching scene is well-formed and imageable with a clear medical prototype, but the nurse and paramedic have been placed in the wrong plausibility levels. Replacing the implausible_hard agent with a truly out-of-place medical professional and reassigning the paramedic to plausible_hard would yield a clean gradient.

While the event and instrument are coherent and there is a clear high-fit professional (car wash worker), washing a car in a driveway is too generic an action: nearly any profession can plausibly do it, so the ‘implausible’ conditions cannot be realized with human professionals. The result is a collapsed gradient in which three of the four agents cluster around the same moderate-to-high plausibility level, indicating that the scene itself needs to be replaced with a more role-specific action to sustain a full plausibility gradient.

The event of writing a research paper with a fountain pen at a wooden desk has a clear academic prototype, appropriate instrument, and is easily depicted in a single image. It cleanly allows for graded thematic fit manipulations via different professional agents.

The scene (breaking a glass window with a hammer in a workshop) is coherent, has a clear prototypical glass-specialist profession, and is easily depictable in a still image. The main weakness is that the chosen plausible_hard agent is very close in plausibility to the glazier, but alternative agents could fix this without altering the scene.

The kitchen–knife–carrot scene is well-formed, prototypically associated with chefs, and easily photographable. The current agent set fails to span the intended plausibility gradient, but alternative agents could readily repair the gradient without changing the scene.

Digging a hole with a shovel in a backyard is a clear, imageable scene with appropriate instrument and strong prototypes (gardener/landscaper). The main issue is misplacing landscaper into an implausible condition; with a better-chosen low-fit but related agent, the gradient would work well.

The scene is well-specified, physically coherent, and strongly anchored in the visual arts/education domain with an appropriate instrument. The main weakness is that the chosen plausible_hard agent is as prototypical as the plausible_easy agent, collapsing the high-fit end of the gradient, but alternative agents could readily fix this.

The event—someone eating a sandwich with their hands in a busy office kitchen—is natural and imageable, with an appropriate instrument. There is a clear prototype class of agents (office workers on a lunch break), but the current selection collapses the two plausible conditions; adjusting the plausible_hard (and possibly refining the implausible_hard) agent would yield a clean plausibility gradient.

The classroom–chalkboard–damp cloth scene is coherent, prototypically associated with teachers, and easily photographable. The main issue is that the chosen implausible_hard agent (musician) is not implausible enough given realistic classroom scenarios, but this can be fixed by choosing a better related-but-wrong school professional.

The event of measuring fabric with a tape measure in a tailor's workshop is clear, strongly associated with tailors, and easy to depict in a single image. The main issues are that the fashion designer is too plausible to function as an implausible_hard agent and that tailor and seamstress are semantically and visually very similar, but these problems can be resolved by choosing better-contrasted agents.

The scene of opening a locked briefcase with a small screwdriver in a dimly lit office is coherent, physically reasonable, and easily photographable, with locksmiths providing a clear prototype. Adjusting the agents (especially reclassifying or replacing the locksmith and security officer) would yield a clean plausibility gradient.

The scene of painting a large mural on a city building with a roller and brush is well-specified, has an obvious prototypical agent, supports a clear plausibility gradient, and can be easily rendered in a single photograph.

The scene 'scooping ice cream with a metal scoop in an ice cream parlor' has an appropriate instrument, a clear prototype (ice cream server), and is straightforward to depict. The main problem is that the chosen implausible_hard agent is still quite plausible; replacing that role with a more clearly mislocated but food-related profession would restore the intended gradient.

The action and instrument are appropriate for basketball, the basketball player is a clear prototype, and the event is easily depictable in a single photo. The chosen agents span a well-ordered plausibility gradient with robust domain relationships.

The kitchen–soup–wooden spoon scenario is well-specified, highly imageable, and has a strong prototype agent. The middle conditions are currently too plausible, but alternative professions are available to restore a clear plausibility gradient.

The NICU scene with a newborn's forehead being gently touched by fingertips is coherent, prototypically associated with neonatal nurses, and easy to depict in a single image. The scene can support a full plausibility gradient with appropriate medical-adjacent but contextually misplaced agents for the implausible_hard slot.

The scene 'washing a car with a sponge in a driveway' is well‑formed, has a clear prototypical agent (the homeowner), and is easily imageable. The current gradient is weakened mainly by misassigned agents and by using a non‑visual role (homeowner); with better‑chosen, more visually distinct professions, the scene can fully support the intended plausibility gradient.

The event ‘writing a letter with a pen at a wooden desk in a quiet study’ is coherent, uses an appropriate instrument, and has a clear prototype (writer). The main weakness is that some non-writing professions can still plausibly be imagined doing this in their off-duty life, so care is needed to choose agents that produce a clear plausibility gradient.

The event 'breaking a windowpane with a hammer in a garage' is coherent and supports a clear window-repair/demolition prototype such as a glazier. The main issue is that mechanic and carpenter are mis-assigned in the top two plausibility levels; with adjusted agents, the gradient would be clean while the implausible levels are already well chosen.

The kitchen-bread-cutting scene is well-formed with a correct instrument and clear food-preparation prototype. The main issue is that the chef is too prototypical to serve as plausible_hard, but alternative agents could readily repair the gradient without changing the scene.

The scene itself is well-formed and imageable, with a clear gardening/yardwork prototype and an appropriate instrument. The only thematic-fit failure is the choice of a chef for implausible_hard; replacing that agent with a profession that digs in a different, non-backyard context would yield a clean four-level gradient.

The scene is well-formed: drawing a portrait with a pencil in an art studio has a clear prototypical agent and is straightforward to depict. The main issue is misplacing the sculptor, who is actually quite plausible for this action, but alternative related professions could readily fill the implausible_hard slot.

While student and teacher provide a good high vs moderate plausibility contrast, the generic nature of ‘eating in a cafeteria’ means almost any professional can plausibly participate in this event, so the lower-plausibility conditions cannot be meaningfully instantiated, and visual distinctiveness is also weak for three of the four roles.

The classroom chalkboard scene with an eraser has a clear prototypical agent and supports a nuanced plausibility gradient with related and unrelated roles. The event is simple to depict visually and semantically coherent across all four conditions.

Measuring the height of a tree with a tape measure in a forest is coherent and photographable, and there is a clear prototype profession (forester). The scene can support plausible_hard agents who are naturally present in forests (e.g., hikers, campers) and implausible_hard agents from related field-science domains, so adjusting the implausible_hard agent would yield a solid gradient.

The scene is well-formed and imageable, with a correct instrument and a strong prototype agent (sommelier), but because opening wine in a dining room is a generic social activity, nearly any profession can plausibly do it, preventing robust low-plausibility conditions.

The event 'painting a mural with a brush on the community center wall' is coherent, uses an appropriate instrument, and has a clear prototypical agent (muralist). The miscalibration lies in the two implausible agents, not in the scene, so replacing them can yield a clean plausibility gradient.

The backyard leaf-scooping scene is clear, physically coherent, and has strong professional prototypes (gardener/landscaper). The main issue is misclassifying a landscaper as implausible; with a better choice for the implausible_hard slot, the gradient would be well-formed. Visually, the only notable problem is that gardener and landscaper are hard to distinguish in images.

The basketball-in-gym scene has a strong prototypical agent, uses an appropriate instrument, and is easy to depict visually. The main issue is that the chosen implausible_hard agent is still quite plausible, but alternative related-sport professionals could repair the gradient.

The kitchen-soup-wooden-spoon scene is well-formed and easily picturable with a strong prototype (chef), but the chosen housewife and nurse agents compress the plausibility gradient by being too plausible. With alternative mid-level and related-but-wrong agents, the scene can cleanly support all four plausibility levels.

The action of touching a basketball with fingers on a court is simple but still anchored in a basketball context with a clear prototypical agent. The scene is easy to depict in a single image and cleanly supports the intended plausibility gradient with distinct professional roles.
The driveway car‑washing scenario is well‑formed and supports a strong prototype and a full plausibility gradient, but all four current agents are misassigned in terms of their plausibility levels.

The action 'writing a letter with a pen on the desk' is too generic and broadly shared across professions to support clear implausible categories; while the instrument and imageability are fine and a prototype profession exists, the plausibility gradient cannot be robustly realized with professional agents.

The scene uses a physically appropriate instrument for breaking and a highly imageable kitchen context. Despite the slightly unusual hammer, a chef remains a clear prototypical agent, and the other professions span a well-ordered gradient from moderately plausible to clearly unrelated.

Although the knife, bread, and kitchen setting are coherent and imageable, the scene is too generic: cutting bread on a kitchen counter is something virtually any adult could plausibly do, so attempts to create implausible agents collapse into ordinary, off-duty cooking scenarios. A more specialized setting (e.g., a commercial bakery, restaurant line, or surgical context with a scalpel) is needed to support a full plausibility gradient.

The scene ‘digging a hole with a shovel in the backyard’ is clear, imageable, and has natural prototype agents (gardener/homeowner). The main problem is misplacing the construction worker in implausible_hard, as this role is actually quite plausible in a backyard context; with alternative agents, the scene can cleanly support all four plausibility levels.

The scene of drawing a portrait with a charcoal pencil in an art studio is well-formed, imageable, and has a strong prototypical agent, but the sculptor is misassigned to an implausible category despite being a plausible visual artist for this action. With adjusted agent choices from teaching/administrative and performing-arts domains, the plausibility gradient would be clearer and more robust.

The event is well-formed and imageable, and it has a clear prototypical agent (office worker), but 'eating a sandwich at his desk' is too generic to strongly constrain professional roles. As a result, the mid-range and low-plausibility conditions collapse, making it hard to construct a clean four-level thematic-fit gradient by varying only the agent’s profession.

The classroom whiteboard scene has a strong prototype (teacher) and can in principle support a full plausibility gradient, but one agent (janitor) is too plausible for its assigned condition and the instrument for erasing is semantically wrong, so the scene specification needs revision.

The scene (measuring a wooden beam with a tape measure on a construction site) is well-formed, has a clear prototypical agent (carpenter), and is easy to depict in a single image. The semantic space around construction and measurement is rich enough to support plausible_hard and implausible_hard roles with better-chosen agents.

The scene of opening a locked wooden door with a key in an old library is coherent, uses an appropriate instrument, and has clear prototypical or near-prototypical professions (librarian, locksmith) for this action. The gradient fails only because the locksmith was placed in an implausible category despite being realistically plausible in this setting.

The backyard fence-painting scene with a wide brush is realistic, has a clear professional prototype (painter), and is easy to depict in a single image; the main issue is that 'carpenter' is too plausible for the intended low-fit level.

The scene uses an appropriate instrument and a highly prototypical profession, is straightforward to depict in a single image, and cleanly supports all four plausibility levels with semantically well-ordered agents.

The event ‘shooting a target with a rifle at the shooting range’ has an appropriate instrument, a clear prototypical profession (marksman/competitive shooter), and is easily captured in a single image. The gradient can be fully supported with better selection of the implausible_hard agent.

The scene uses an appropriate instrument and a highly prototypical cooking context, is easily photographable, and affords a well-spaced plausibility gradient with multiple alternative agents available for each level if needed.

The NICU scene with a newborn and fingertip touch is well-formed, clearly imageable, and has a strong medical prototype. The current agent assignments blur the plausible tiers but can be corrected by swapping in better-suited professions for the mid-plausibility levels.

The car-washing-in-a-driveway scene uses an appropriate instrument and has a clear car-care prototype, and it is easy to depict in a single image. The main problem is that the chosen implausible_hard agent is too plausible, but alternative car-related professions could fix the gradient without changing the scene structure.

The scene—writing a letter with a fountain pen at a wooden desk—is well-formed, prototypically linked to secretarial/office work and easily picturable. The gradient is undermined by misplacing a highly compatible agent (calligrapher) into an implausible slot, but alternative professions could repair the gradient without changing the core event.

The demolition-at-construction-site scene is coherent, uses an appropriate instrument, and has a clear prototype profession, but the chosen implausible_hard agent is too plausible. With a better-chosen related-but-wrong professional, the thematic gradient would be strong, though visual distinctiveness among multiple construction roles remains a concern.

Cutting a customer's hair with scissors in a hair salon is a well-defined, imageable scene with a clear prototypical agent and appropriate instrument; only the mid-plausibility agents need reassignment to sharpen the gradient.

The cemetery grave-digging scene is well-formed: a shovel is an appropriate instrument, there is a clear prototype profession (gravedigger), and the full plausibility gradient can be instantiated with suitable agents. The main weakness lies not in thematic structure but in visual similarity between the two cemetery-worker roles.

The art-studio drawing scene is well-formed, prototypical, and easily photographable, but the psychology researcher and sculptor are misassigned on the plausibility scale. With better-chosen adjacent-domain agents, the gradient would be clean and interpretable.

The verb–scene combination (eating a gourmet steak at a fine-dining table) has a clear prototype and is easy to picture, but because almost any professional can plausibly appear as a diner, it cannot reliably sustain a four-level agent plausibility gradient; implausible_hard collapses into plausible_hard, and two professions also lack strong visual iconicity.

The educational whiteboard scene has a strong prototype and can support a clear plausibility gradient, but the instrument choice ('with a dry-erase marker') is semantically inappropriate for erasing, so the sentence template should be revised while keeping the same general scene and agents.

The hospital blood-pressure scene is well-formed, with an appropriate instrument and a clear prototypical agent (nurse), and is easy to depict visually. The main issue is misplacement of a surgeon into an implausible category rather than choosing a more clearly non-bedside medical professional.

The bank vault scene with a keycard provides a clear, concrete action and setting with a strong prototypical agent and room for semantically related but incorrect agents. The only concern lies in visual similarity between some white-collar roles, not in the underlying thematic-fit structure.

The scene uses an appropriate instrument for painting, has a clear prototypical profession (artist), is straightforward to depict in a single image, and supports a well-spaced plausibility gradient; any issues arise from minor visual similarity between specific chosen agents, not from the scene design itself.

The scene—scooping ice cream with a metal scoop at an ice cream shop counter—is well-formed, has a clear prototype (ice cream server), uses the right instrument, and is easily photographed. The main problem is that the chosen implausible_hard agent is still quite plausible, but alternative related professions could fill that role and restore the gradient.

The basketball scene is well-formed with an appropriate instrument and a clear prototype agent; the main issue is that the chosen implausible_hard agent is too plausible, but this can be fixed by selecting a less natural yet still sports-related profession.

The restaurant-kitchen stirring scene is well-formed with a clear chef prototype and an appropriate instrument, and it can support the full plausibility gradient. The main issues are the over-plausibility and visual similarity of the pastry chef to the main chef, which can be resolved by choosing a different, related-but-wrong profession for implausible_hard.

The abdominal examination scene with a gloved hand in an exam room is clear, imageable, and has a strong prototypical agent, with coherent related and unrelated professions populating all four plausibility levels; only minor visual similarity arises between the family doctor and medical student images.

The scene uses an appropriate instrument and a very clear prototypical profession, is straightforward to depict in a single image, and naturally supports all four plausibility levels with distinct thematic fits. Any minor visual ambiguity arises from agent selection (two generic car-service roles) rather than from flaws in the underlying scene design.

The scene of writing a prescription with a pen at a hospital desk is prototypically medical, with a clear doctor prototype and an appropriate instrument and setting. The main issue is that the pharmacist is too plausible for the implausible_hard category, but this can be fixed by swapping in a more peripherally related hospital professional.

The construction/demolition scenario is strong and supports a full plausibility gradient, but the bricklayer is misclassified as implausible_hard and the demolition versus construction worker distinction is both conceptually and visually subtle; revising the implausible_hard agent and making the high-fit and medium-fit agents more distinct would improve the stimuli.

The event 'brushing a child’s hair with a hairbrush in a salon' is concrete, uses an appropriate instrument, and has a clear prototype (hairstylist). The main issues are the misplacement of the firefighter as implausible_hard and the visual unidentifiability of the parent, both of which can be addressed by choosing better agents rather than redesigning the scene.

The scene is concrete, uses an appropriate instrument, has a clear prototypical profession, and affords a robust plausibility gradient with visually distinguishable, role-based differences in plausibility.

The forest brush-burning scene with a flamethrower has a clear prototypical agent (wildland firefighter), supports plausible and implausible roles with a good semantic gradient, and is easily photographable. The main issue is the visual identifiability of the implausible_easy agent, not the scene itself.

The cemetery-burial scene is concrete, imageable, and has an obvious core professional (cemetery gravedigger), but the current assignment misplaces three of the four agents and uses a visually non-distinct funeral director; with better-chosen, visually distinct roles the full plausibility gradient can be supported.

The ‘carrying a suitcase at airport baggage claim’ scene is concrete and imageable, and there are professions for whom handling suitcases here is clearly core. The main issues are the misplacement of the firefighter in implausible_hard and the use of a visually unidentifiable social role (‘passenger’) as plausible_easy; both can be remedied by choosing more appropriate, uniformed agents within the same scene.

The action 'catching a fish with a fishing rod on a fishing pier' is clear, concrete, and has a strong prototype (fisherman), and the setting is easy to depict in a single image; only the implausible_easy role is not semantically distant enough from fishing.

Semantically, the event 'combing a child’s hair with a comb in a bathroom' has a strong prototype (parent) and can support all four plausibility levels with better-chosen agents. But because the prototypical role is a non-uniformed caregiver, the plausible_easy agent cannot be made visually identifiable in line with the experimental constraints. To satisfy both thematic and visual requirements, the scene likely needs redesign (e.g., shifting to a salon/hairdresser-centered setting) rather than just swapping agents.

The orchestra-conducting scene is clear, prototypical, and uses an appropriate instrument (baton). However, the chosen plausible_hard agent is too close in role and appearance to the conductor, collapsing the top two plausibility levels; replacing that agent with a genuinely secondary-but-plausible role would fix the gradient.

The restaurant-kitchen steak-cooking scene is concrete, imageable, and has a strong prototypical agent with an appropriate instrument. The main problems are that the line cook is too prototypical for plausible_hard, the firefighter lacks sufficient overlap for implausible_hard, and the librarian is not visually identifiable as a profession without context.

The salon hair-curling scene is concrete, imageable, and has a strong prototypical agent. The only major issue is the choice of implausible_hard agent (chef), which lacks sufficient domain overlap and behaves as a clear-no case similar to the firefighter.

The hair-salon hair-cutting scene is concrete, physically appropriate, and easily depicted, but the chosen plausible_hard and implausible_hard agents do not optimally instantiate the intermediate plausibility levels; suitable replacement agents are readily available.

The action 'digging a hole with a shovel on a construction site' is concrete, imageable, and has a clear core professional. Thematic gradation across agents is well-formed; remaining issues mainly concern the visual similarity between industrial labor roles rather than the scene design.

The scene itself—drawing blood with a needle in a hospital—is clear, concrete, and supports a full plausibility gradient. The main issues are the closeness in plausibility between phlebotomist and nurse and the somewhat ambiguous visual identifiability of a phlebotomist; these can be addressed by adjusting agent choices or visual prompts without changing the underlying scene.

The machine-shop drilling scene is concrete, has a clear prototypical agent, uses an appropriate instrument, and cleanly supports all four plausibility levels with visually distinguishable roles. Minor ambiguity in how precisely some trades are labeled does not undermine the gradient or overall scene quality.

Although drinking a beer at a bar is a natural scenario, the default agent is a generic patron with no distinctive visual identity, and many other professions can plausibly appear as bar patrons off duty, making it difficult to construct clear implausible_hard and implausible_easy cases while satisfying the identifiability requirement.

The living-room dusting scene is concrete, uses an appropriate instrument, and has a clear prototype (housekeeper). The main issue is that the carpenter is too plausible to serve as an implausible_hard agent; replacing this role with a related but clearly mis-situated cleaner-type profession would yield a robust plausibility gradient.

The event 'eating a hot dog with hands in a baseball stadium' is simple, concrete, and easily imaged, and there is a clear prototypical role (a fan/spectator). The main issues arise from mis-assignment of specific agents to plausibility levels and from choosing an implausible_hard agent (chef) that is actually fairly plausible and lacks the required multi-dimensional overlap with the plausible_easy agent.

The classroom-with-whiteboard scene and the use of an eraser are appropriate and have a clear prototypical agent (teacher), but the chosen implausible agents are misassigned and one (graphic designer) lacks a distinct visual identity.

The bottle is an appropriate instrument for feeding a lion cub, the zookeeper is an unambiguous prototype, and the event is straightforward to depict in a single photo. The zoo‑animal‑care domain provides ample room for a graded plausibility spectrum with both related and unrelated professions.

The boxing-ring fistfight scene has a clear prototype (boxer), supports a graded set of related and unrelated roles, and is easy to depict in a single image; the main weakness is the choice of a visually non-iconic implausible agent rather than the scene itself.

The fishing-with-rod-on-a-lake scene is concrete, has a clear prototype (angler), and easily supports all four plausibility levels. The main weakness is visual: the ‘fashion model’ role is not reliably identifiable from appearance alone and should be replaced with a more visually canonical but semantically unrelated profession.

The basic scene—gluing two wooden planks with a glue gun in a woodworking workshop—is concrete, physically coherent, and has a clear prototype (a woodworker/carpenter). The current agents do not optimally realize the plausibility gradient, but suitable replacements exist, so the scene itself is sound.

The kitchen-cheese-grater scene is concrete, has an appropriate instrument, and a clear prototype (chef) and can support a full plausibility gradient. However, the chosen implausible_hard agent is too plausible, and the implausible_easy agent lacks a visually distinctive profession, so agents should be revised.

The action and instrument are appropriate and concrete, the hotel laundry station naturally supports a housekeeping prototype, and related garment-care professionals allow for graded plausibility distinctions without compromising physical plausibility.

Knitting a sweater with needles and yarn at home is a clear, imageable scene with an obvious knitting-specialist prototype. The only serious semantic issue is the choice of carpenter for implausible_hard; replacing that agent with a more closely related but still wrong textile/clothing profession would yield a cleaner gradient. Visually, the first two agents risk looking similar as generic knitters unless their role markers are strengthened.

The action (lighting a birthday cake with a match on a dining table) is concrete, visually simple, and has a reasonable prototype (parent/host), but current agents misplace that prototype and choose an implausible_hard agent with insufficient overlap. With better-chosen, visually distinct roles, the scene can support the full plausibility gradient.

The ER chart-reading scene with a penlight is concrete, imageable, and has a clear prototype (doctor/nurse), and the instrument is physically appropriate. The main issue is that nurse is too prototypical for the action, collapsing the top two plausibility levels; replacing the plausible_hard agent would fix the gradient while preserving strong visual distinctiveness.

The action, instrument, and setting are coherent and easily photographed, with a strong prototypical agent (carpenter). The main weakness is that the chosen implausible_hard agent (welder) is still too plausible; replacing that role with a more clearly mismatched but related profession would yield a clean four-level gradient.

The core action and setting (melting a chocolate bar with a hairdryer on a kitchen counter) are physically plausible and imageable with a clear culinary prototype in the pastry chef. The main issue is that the chosen implausible_hard agent (welder) lacks sufficient multi-dimensional overlap with the pastry chef, but this can be corrected by substituting a more appropriately related yet wrong-domain profession.

The action, instrument, and setting are appropriate, and a postal worker provides a clear prototypical agent. However, using a generic 'customer' both compresses the top end of the plausibility range and fails the visual identifiability requirement. Replacing the customer with a visually distinctive, moderately related profession would make this scene suitable for the intended experiment.

The action of painting a wooden fence with a roller in a backyard is clear, prototypically associated with a painter, and easily photographable. The main issues are the over-plausibility of the carpenter for implausible_hard and the lack of a visually identifiable marker for ‘homeowner’; both can be addressed by choosing alternative agents without changing the basic scene.

The kitchen-peeling scene is conceptually and visually coherent with a clear culinary prototype and appropriate instrument, but the selected agents do not realize the intended four-level plausibility gradient, and one agent (home cook) lacks a distinctive visual identity.

The medical exam room with skin pinched using sterilized tweezers is coherent, imageable, and has a clear medical prototype. The only weakness is the somewhat thin conceptual linkage of the jewelry designer as an implausible_hard foil, which can be remedied by selecting a more strongly overlapping non-medical profession.

The community-garden planting scene is concrete, imageable, and has a strong prototypical agent and correct instrument, but the chosen implausible agents are too plausible; with better-chosen agents, the full plausibility gradient would be well supported.

The kitchen–water–pitcher scene is concrete, physically coherent, and supports a clear professional prototype (waiter) with room for related but incorrect roles. The current agents are miscategorized and the librarian lacks a distinctive visual identity, but these problems can be resolved by reassigning and/or replacing agents without changing the underlying scene.

The action, instrument, and location are concrete and appropriate, and a gardener is a clear prototype. However, the landscaper is too close to the gardener in role, collapsing the top two plausibility levels; and the firefighter as implausible_hard is somewhat borderline though workable. Better-chosen agents could cleanly support all four plausibility levels.

The carpentry workshop plus handsaw and wooden plank provide a concrete, imageable scene with a clear prototypical agent and a workable plausibility gradient; the only minor concern is that the librarian’s visual identity is somewhat ambiguous but still serviceable.

The core scene—scooping dirt with a shovel on a construction site—is concrete, has a clear prototype (construction worker), and is easy to photograph. The main issues are the choice of chef for implausible_hard (too unrelated) and librarian for implausible_easy (not visually identifiable); both can be fixed by substituting more suitable roles without changing the scene.

The sewing-a-quilt-in-a-sewing-studio scene is concrete, with a clear prototypical agent (quilter) and appropriate instrument. The only issue is that the chosen implausible_hard agent is too unrelated, but alternative agents exist that would fix the gradient.

Shaving a man’s beard with a straight razor in a barbershop uses an appropriate instrument, has a clear prototypical professional (barber), is easy to depict in a single photograph, and supports a well-ordered plausibility gradient from highly typical to clearly unrelated agents.

The underlying scene—someone shooting a basketball on a court—has a clear prototype and supports a full plausibility gradient, but the instrument phrase is malformed and the chosen implausible_easy profession lacks a distinctive visual identity, so both the sentence and at least one agent need revision.

The bakery–cake–spatula scene is concrete, imageable, and has a strong prototypical agent, but the current choices for plausible_hard and implausible_hard do not support a clear plausibility gradient; appropriate alternative agents could fix this without changing the basic scene.

The cooking scene (stirring soup with a wooden spoon on a stove) is concrete, uses an appropriate instrument, and clearly supports a chef as the prototype. The current implausible_hard agent lacks sufficient semantic overlap with the chef, but appropriate replacement agents from related food domains exist, so the scene itself is sound and only needs agent substitution.

The core scene (construction worker building something with a hammer on a construction site) is well-chosen and highly imageable, but 'a brick chimney' is too plausible for implausible_hard and 'a wooden shed' is nearly as prototypical as the wall frame, so the current patient set does not provide a clean plausibility gradient even though the template itself is solid.

The core scene (chef using a blowtorch in a kitchen) is strong and imageable, with a clear prototypical object. The main problem is the solder joint, which is both thematically too remote and visually technical; replacing it with a kitchen-related but non-burn-target object would yield a robust gradient.

The burial-in-a-cemetery scene with a gravedigger and shovel is strong and has a clear prototype (coffin). The current patients mostly respect the intended plausibility gradient, though the concrete pipe is borderline between plausible_hard and implausible_hard. With minor patient adjustments, the scene can yield a very clean gradient.

The core scene—mail carrier carrying something with his arms on a sidewalk—is well-chosen, imageable, and has a clear prototype. Visual identifiability is excellent. The main issues are that the small cardboard box is too prototypical to be plausible_hard, and the fire extinguisher is better treated as a rare but plausible object rather than implausible_hard; the implausible_easy piano also leans heavily on physical impossibility.

The scene of a pitcher catching objects with a glove on a baseball diamond is coherent and strongly tied to the verb ‘catch’. The instrument and agent fit naturally, there is a clear prototypical object (baseball), and the chosen patients span a well-ordered plausibility gradient while remaining visually distinct and depictable in a single photograph.

The barbershop combing scene is conceptually strong, with a clear prototype and natural use of the verb and instrument. The current patients yield a good plausibility gradient, though the cat’s fur case sits borderline between plausible_hard and implausible_hard and could be refined if a sharper distinction is needed.

The musical conducting scene is thematically coherent and visually strong, but the plausible patients are all groups of people, violating the no-people-as-patients constraint, and one plausible item ('choir') is mispositioned as plausible_hard while the implausible_hard item ('train') lacks the required graded overlap. The verb sense and agent-role are fine, yet to satisfy the experimental constraints and obtain a clean gradient, the entire scene should be redesigned around a different sense of 'conduct' with non-human patients.

Core scene (chef cooking with spatula on stovetop) is strong, imageable, and supports a clear prototype. The current patients, however, cluster three highly plausible foods together, undermining the intended plausibility gradient.

Overall, the scene (barber curling hair with a curling iron in a barbershop) is coherent, imageable, and supports a clear prototype plus a plausible non-prototypical object, with two semantically distant implausible objects; only the curtain item is somewhat borderline but still defensible as implausible_hard.

The barbershop cutting scene is well-formed and imageable with a clear prototype, and the agent is action-prototypical. The only issue is that 'a piece of paper' is too plausible to serve as implausible_hard; replacing it with a barbershop-related but non-cut target would restore a clean plausibility gradient.

The core scene—construction worker digging with a shovel in a trench—is strong, prototypical, and easily imageable with a clear prototype patient (dirt). Visual identifiability is excellent. The only issue is thematic misplacement of the buried cable, which should be treated as plausible rather than implausible; substituting a more clearly wrong but context-related object would yield a full, clean gradient.

While the images would be visually clear and the agent/instrument are appropriate, the verb 'draw' with a schoolchild on a sketchpad does not support a strong plausibility gradient: almost any concrete object is a feasible drawing subject, and there is no clear prototype patient. The scene therefore cannot reliably yield distinct plausible vs. implausible levels and should be redesigned with a more constrained action context.

The core dental drilling scene is strong and easily imageable, with an appropriate agent and instrument and a clear prototype (tooth), but the current plausible_hard item is too prototypical and the implausible_hard item is only borderline, so the gradient needs patient revisions rather than a scene redesign.

Conceptually, the scene is strong: the agent, verb, instrument, and location are well chosen, and the four patients support a clear plausibility gradient. However, the two oil patients are visually less canonical in a glass and the sommelier’s role is somewhat hard to distinguish from a generic waiter, so modest patient and styling adjustments would improve experimental robustness.

The dusting-on-a-bookshelf scene is thematically coherent and visually clear, but dusting is so broadly applicable that many different objects (including the proposed 'implausible' ones) remain quite plausible as dusting targets. This collapses the gradient and makes it hard to obtain clear implausible conditions without violating the experiment's constraints.

The core scene—schoolchild eating with a fork in a cafeteria—is strong and imageable, with a clear prototypical food object. Only the ordering of the two implausible patients is problematic; replacing or reassigning those objects would yield a valid four-level plausibility gradient.

The core scene—warehouse worker with an eraser correcting pencil marks on a box-related item—is coherent, imageable, and has a clear prototype, but the low-plausibility patients as currently assigned are mis-placed and too similar in domain to the plausible items; with revised implausible_hard and implausible_easy objects, the gradient would be much cleaner.

A zookeeper feeding primates with a bucket is a clear, concrete scene with a strong prototype and ample room for gradations of plausibility based on the type of object being fed. The only minor limitation is that zookeeper attire alone may be somewhat ambiguous without context, but within the enclosure scene the role will be obvious.

The scene is thematically coherent and visually workable, but the implausible_hard choice ('a punching bag') is too plausible, and the canonical patient is a human opponent, which violates the constraint against people as patients. Because no non-human object can serve as a genuine prototype for a boxer fighting in a ring, the scene should be redesigned (e.g., different verb/agent or location) to support the required gradient under the constraints.

The core scene (fisherman fishing with a rod in a river) is well chosen and easily photographable, with a clear prototypical object. However, catfish and crayfish are both too plausible as rod-caught river animals, so the intended plausibility gradient is not realized; alternative patients could easily fix this.

The carpenter–glue gun–workbench setup is coherent and has a clear prototypical patient (wood) and several nearby material types for graded plausibility. However, the current mid-level items do not form a clean yes/no boundary: the ceramic tile is too plausible for implausible_hard relative to the cardboard box.

This is a strong, concrete kitchen scene with a very clear prototype (cheese) and a physically appropriate instrument and agent. The primary minor issue is that the plausible_hard item (carrot) is almost as prototypical as the cheese, but this is a matter of patient selection rather than scene design.

The core laundry-ironing scene is coherent, imageable, and has a strong prototypical object, but the current implausible_hard choice is actually a normal ironing target and collapses into the plausible range; adjusting that patient (and perhaps choosing a slightly less typical plausible_hard garment) would yield a robust plausibility gradient.

The knitting scene with a grandmother and knitting needles on her lap is strong, concrete, and imageable, with a clear prototypical object (a scarf). However, the woolen blanket is far too plausible to serve as implausible_hard, and the hat is nearly as prototypical as the scarf, compressing the gradient. Replacing the implausible_hard patient (and possibly choosing a less prototypical plausible_hard item) would yield a well-structured gradient.

Conceptually, the verb–agent–instrument–location combination is coherent and has a clear prototype patient, but three of the four patients are misassigned along the plausibility gradient. The main experimental weakness is not the plausibility structure but the visual unidentifiability of the ‘candle maker’ as a distinct social role.

Conceptually, the agent and instrument fit the verb, and the scene is easy to picture, but the verb 'look' plus an art-gallery setting makes thematic fit differences too subtle for a robust four-level plausibility gradient, and the agent’s profession is not visually identifiable.

The tailoring/fitting scene with a measuring tape is well chosen and easily imageable, and it can support a full plausibility gradient. However, the most canonical patient for this specific setup is a dress form on the fitting stand, not a bolt of fabric, so the plausible_easy and plausible_hard patients should be swapped or otherwise adjusted.

Conceptually, the chef-at-stovetop-melting scene is strong and easily imageable with a clear prototype object (butter) and an action-prototypical agent and instrument. The current patient choices produce a somewhat compressed gradient at both the plausible and implausible ends, but this can be remedied by swapping in better-contrasted non-prototypical and non-food objects without changing the basic scene.

Semantically, a librarian opening things on a library desk is a strong scene with a clear prototype and room for a graded plausibility manipulation. However, the non-prototypical patients are mis-assigned, and visually the choice of 'librarian' as agent is problematic because the role lacks distinctive attire.

Core scene design (artist painting with a brush in a studio) is strong and imageable with a clear prototypical object. The main issue is that the chosen implausible_hard patient is actually quite plausible; replacing it with a more clearly wrong but context-related object would yield a well-structured gradient.

The core scene—bank teller paying with cash at a bank counter—is coherent and imageable, with a clear canonical patient available, but the chosen patients misalign with the intended plausibility levels and do not produce a clean gradient. The agent’s visual identifiability is somewhat weak but not fatally so.

The core scene (chef peeling something with a peeler on a kitchen counter) is strong and image-friendly, with a clear prototype (potato) and ample room for related and unrelated objects. The only issue is that a carrot is too prototypical to serve as plausible_hard; the implausible conditions are well chosen and visually distinct.

Core scene (nurse pinching something on a patient’s arm with her fingers) is well-chosen and imageable with a clear prototype (skin fold). The visual roles are identifiable and distinct; the main issue is that the lower two plausibility levels are mis-assigned, not that the scene is fundamentally flawed.

The scene is conceptually strong and easily photographed, with a good prototype and a meaningful related-but-wrong object (potato). The main weakness is that the current plausible_hard choice is almost as canonical as the plausible_easy item, so slight patient adjustments could improve the plausibility gradient.

Core scene design is solid: bartender and pouring are tightly linked, the bar counter and hand-as-instrument are appropriate, and there is a clear prototypical object (alcohol bottle). Core scene (groundskeeper raking in a park) is strong and easily photographed, with a clear prototypical object (leaves). The core scene (carpenter sawing with a handsaw in a workshop) is strong, prototypical, and visually clear, with a well-defined prototype patient (a 2x4). The only issues are the swapped implausible_hard and implausible_easy patients; correcting those choices will yield a clean plausibility gradient without changing the scene.

The scene is conceptually strong and imageable, with an action-prototypical agent and a clear prototypical patient. The main problems are at the implausible end (sand vs cat litter) and the visual indistinguishability between vanilla ice cream and frozen yogurt; these can be resolved by choosing better-contrasted patients.

The scene of a tailor sewing at a sewing table is strongly coherent, easily photographed, and supports a clear plausibility gradient from prototypical garment work through related but wrong-domain footwear to clearly unrelated electronics. The barbershop shaving scene is strong, concrete, and easily photographable, with a clear canonical object for shaving and several related and unrelated objects available. The current patient assignments mis-order the goat's beard and mustache, but appropriate reassignment would yield a robust plausibility gradient without changing the core scene.

The scene is well-chosen: the agent is strongly linked to the action 'shoot' in this context, the instrument and location are appropriate, and the patients span a clean plausibility gradient while remaining visually distinct and easily recognizable.

Conceptually, spreading something on toast is an excellent domain with a clear prototype (butter) and room for less typical spreads and unrelated objects, but using a waiter as the fixed agent is not action-prototypical for 'spreading'; a chef/cook would be more appropriate. The chef-stirring-in-a-pot scene is well chosen with a clear prototype (soup) and a good plausible alternative (batter), plus a clearly absurd brick case. Conceptually, a pitcher swatting something with his glove on the mound is coherent and imageable, with a clear prototype (a baseball). The core scene—janitor sweeping with a broom in a school hallway—is strong, imageable, and supports a clear prototype and a good plausibility gradient. The only issue is the dust bunny being too plausible for the implausible_hard slot; replacing it with a more category-mismatched but related hallway object would fix the gradient.

Core scene design is sound: a seamstress threading something with a needle at a sewing machine has an obvious prototype (thread) and supports related-but-wrong items like a shoelace and unrelated items like a pencil. The main issue is that embroidery floss is effectively just another kind of thread, collapsing the top two plausibility levels, but this can be resolved by choosing a more clearly non-prototypical yet still plausible textile object.

The scene of a pitcher throwing on a baseball diamond with his arm is well-formed, action-prototypical, and easily photographed. The chosen patients span from canonical to categorically unrelated while maintaining recognizable visual differences and a smooth plausibility gradient.

Core scene elements (nurse, pediatric ward, finger tickling, child body parts) are strong and imageable; the main issue is the choice of implausible_hard patient, which currently behaves like a clearly implausible object rather than a borderline one.

The scene of a referee touching an object on a soccer field is coherent, easy to depict, and supports a full plausibility gradient using sports-related and non-sports objects. The core scene (tow truck driver towing something by cable on a highway) is strong and supports a clear prototype. Conceptually, the scene is sound for 'type': a secretary at her desk with a keyboard typing a document is natural, and suitable alternative patients exist for all four plausibility levels. The core scene (janitor vacuuming with a vacuum cleaner in a school hallway) is well-formed and imageable, but the plausibility gradient is weakened by a non-prototypical plausible_easy patient and a borderline implausible_hard patient.

Semantically, a dishwasher washing items with a sponge in a kitchen is a strong, well-structured scene with a clear prototypical patient, but the current plausible_hard choice is mis-placed and the implausible_hard choice is borderline; these can be remedied by selecting more suitable patients. The separate visual issue is that the agent role 'dishwasher' lacks a distinctive appearance.

The scene is conceptually strong and visually clear, with an appropriate agent, action, and instrument, and a well-defined prototypical object (surveillance monitor). Core scene (gardener watering in a garden) is strong and supports the full plausibility gradient; only the implausible_hard choice fails the multi-dimensional overlap requirement.

The core scene of a postal worker weighing items on a digital scale at a counter is strong, prototypical, and easy to depict. The core scene—receptionist writing with a pen on a desk—is sound and has a clear prototypical object, but the current choice of a whiteboard as implausible_hard is miscalibrated because it is itself a normal writing surface. Conceptually, a janitor in a school hallway using a mop handle to break things is somewhat atypical but workable, with a light bulb providing a natural prototype target; the main problems are the misplacement of the frozen pipe, light bulb, and smartphone along the plausibility gradient rather than the scene itself.

Dentist + toothbrush + dental chair is a strong, easily imageable scene with a clear prototype (a tooth/teeth). The two plausible patients are misordered and very close in plausibility, but the implausible items are well chosen and all objects are visually distinct and identifiable.

The core scene (construction worker building with a hammer on a site) is well-chosen and imageable, with a clear prototypical patient and many nearby objects for gradient manipulation. The only problems are the mis-assignment of the mid-level patients, not the scene itself.

The chef-with-torch-on-kitchen-counter scene is strong: the agent and instrument are action-prototypical, the prototype patient is clear, and the plausibility gradient is well-separated with good semantic and visual contrasts.

Semantically, the scene is strong: a grave digger burying things in a cemetery with a shovel naturally supports a clear prototype and a plausibility gradient. The main weakness is the borderline status of the car engine as implausible_hard and, separately, the fact that 'grave digger' is not visually distinctive as a profession, which is a visual-design issue rather than a thematic one.

Core scene design is strong: the agent, action, instrument, and location are well-matched and easily depicted in a photo, with a clear prototypical object. The current implausible_hard choice is too plausible, but the scene itself can support a full plausibility gradient with adjusted patients.

The firefighting rescue-on-a-ledge scene with gloved hands is clear, imageable, and visually strong. However, the brick and fire extinguisher are mis-ordered in terms of plausibility; with alternative patients or reassignment, this scene can support a sharp plausibility gradient.

Core scene design (hairdresser combing something with a comb in a salon) is strong and supports a clear prototype and visually robust gradient; only the implausible_hard patient needs replacement to sharpen the plausibility contrast.

The chef–stovetop–spatula scenario is a strong, prototypical cooking scene with a clear canonical patient and good space for related but wrong and clearly unrelated objects. It is easily captured in a single image and supports a clean plausibility gradient.

Conceptually, a barber curling hair in a barbershop is sound and supports a plausibility gradient, but specifying scissors as the curling instrument is non-prototypical for the verb. The barbershop cutting scene is conceptually strong and visually clear, but the choice and ordering of patients do not currently realize the intended plausibility gradient; in particular, the prototype object is missing and the two implausible conditions are reversed. This is a strong, concrete scene with a highly prototypical agent-verb pairing, a clear prototype patient (dirt), and good semantic space around it to support a full plausibility gradient. The artist–drawing–pencil–sketchpad scene is natural and visually clear, but because an artist can reasonably draw almost any concrete object, all four patients come out plausible and the intended gradient collapses. The scene cannot support clear implausible levels under the given constraints.

This is a well-chosen dental drilling scene with a clear prototypical object and a reasonable plausible_hard object, but the implausible_hard patient is too unrelated and collapses with the implausible_easy case. The bar scene with a bartender drinking from vessels is coherent, the agent and instrument fit the verb, and there is a clear prototype drinking vessel. The housekeeping/dusting-at-a-bookshelf scenario is coherent, the agent and instrument are well chosen, and all elements are easily depictable. Conceptually, a teacher erasing marks with a cloth on a whiteboard is a strong, imageable scene with a clear prototypical patient, but 'chalk marks' and 'crayon marks' are mispositioned along the plausibility gradient. The zookeeper-lion-feeding-with-pole scene is conceptually strong, has an obvious prototypical object (meat), uses an appropriate instrument, and supports a clear plausibility gradient from meat to toy to textbook while remaining easily depictable in a single photograph.

The scene uses an action-prototypical agent and instrument in an appropriate location with a clear training prototype (heavy bag). The core fishing scene is strong: agent, verb, instrument, and location are all well chosen and easy to depict. The visual distinctness and identifiability of all objects are excellent; only the middle-level implausible_hard patient needs revision to create a cleaner plausibility gradient.

The core scene—carpenter gluing with a glue gun in a workshop—is strong and imageable with a clear prototypical patient. The scene concept (laundry worker ironing on a board) is thematically strong and supports a clear prototype and a plausible vs. implausible gradient, but the selected implausible_hard patient is misclassified, and the agent’s profession is not visually distinctive, which would limit experimental usability without redesign of the agent role.

The knitting-in-convent scene with a nun and knitting needles is conceptually coherent, visually imageable, and has a clear prototypical object (a scarf). The scene of a streetlamp technician using a remote on a city sidewalk cleanly supports a prototypical target (streetlight), a plausible extension (porch light), and graded implausible objects (car headlight, toothbrush). The tailor-measuring-with-tape-measure-in-shop scene is strong and imageable with a clear prototype, but the current low-plausibility patients are misordered, and the fabric object is almost as prototypical as the arm, slightly weakening the gradient. The melting-in-a-saucepan-by-a-chef scene is well designed and highly imageable; only the candle as implausible_hard is somewhat borderline relative to implausible_easy, but alternative patients could readily fix this.

This is a strong, concrete kitchen-preparation scene with a prototypical agent, instrument, and patient, and it naturally yields a full gradient of plausibility while keeping patients visually distinct and easily recognizable.

The gardener-planting-in-garden scene is conceptually solid, with a correct agent and instrument and an obvious prototype patient. The scene of a groundskeeper raking in a park is strong and highly imageable with a clear prototypical patient (leaf pile). This is a strong, well-structured scene: the agent and instrument are highly appropriate, the prototype patient is clear, and the four patients span a clean plausibility gradient with good semantic structure and visual distinctness.

This is a strong, prototypical shaving scene with a clear prototype (man’s beard), good visual clarity, and a meaningful plausibility gradient, though the top two conditions are quite similar in plausibility.

Core scene (chef spreading something with a spatula on bread) is strong, natural, and highly imageable, with a clear prototypical object. The core scene—tailor threading something with a needle at a sewing table—is coherent and imageable, with an action-prototypical agent and instrument. This is a strong baseball-pitching scene with an action-prototypical agent and instrument, a very clear prototype patient (baseball), and well-spaced plausibility levels using sports-related and non-sports objects; all elements are easily depicted and recognized in a single photograph.

The tow-truck-on-highway scenario with a steel cable provides a clear, imageable context and a strong prototype object. The warehouse scene with a heavy wooden crate and arm-carrying is coherent, imageable, and has a clear prototype (warehouse worker). The main issue is that the chosen implausible_hard agent is too plausible, but alternative related professions could fix this while maintaining a robust gradient.

The scene of catching a baseball with a glove on a baseball diamond is concrete, easily imageable, and has a strong prototypical agent. While the instrument and basic visual setup are fine and easy to photograph, hair-combing at a vanity is a universal everyday action not tied to any profession, so all four roles appear similarly plausible; the scene should be redesigned to make the action occupationally specific (e.g., styling a client’s hair in a salon) to support clear plausibility contrasts.

The orchestral conducting scene with a baton in a concert hall is well-defined, has a clear prototype (conductor), and is easy to depict. The cooking-soup-in-a-kitchen scene is concrete, visually simple, and strongly associated with a chef while allowing related but less appropriate restaurant staff and unrelated professionals to form a clear plausibility gradient.

The basic event (curling a barbell in a gym) is clear and imageable with an appropriate instrument and a strong prototype (weightlifter). A different verb/patient/location combination with a more domain-specific activity would better support the full four-level plausibility gradient.

Cutting a loaf of bread with a serrated knife on a kitchen counter is a well-defined, concrete scene with an obvious food-preparation prototype. The main issues arise from agent selection (housewife too plausible and barber too weakly related) and one visually unidentifiable role, not from any flaw in the underlying scene.

The backyard-digging scene with a shovel is concrete, imageable, and has a strong prototype (gardener/landscaper). The main issues are the misplacement of the construction worker in implausible_hard and the poor visual identifiability of the homeowner; both can be remedied by choosing different agents.

The art-studio drawing scene is concrete, has an obvious prototype (artist), and is easy to depict. The main problem is that 'sculptor' is too plausible for implausible_hard; replacing that agent with a related-but-wrong professional from the arts domain would fix the gradient.

The machine-shop drilling scene is concrete, has a clear prototypical agent (machinist), and is easy to depict in a single image. The plausibility gradient can be supported, but the current implausible_hard agent must be replaced with someone from a related trade who does not naturally belong in a machine shop.

Although the medical agents and dancer are visually distinct and identifiable, the underlying event – drinking water by a hospital bedside – is too generic and not anchored in any profession-specific activity. The scene itself is well-formed and supports a clear plausibility gradient, but the choice of 'homeowner' creates a visual identifiability failure; replacing that agent with a role that has a clearer visual identity would yield a strong set of stimuli.

While 'office worker eating a sandwich at his desk' is intuitively clear, the action is so generic that many professions can fill the role without strong plausibility differences, and at least one role (librarian) lacks a recognizable visual identity. To support a robust gradient, a more job-specific action/instrument/location combination is needed (e.g., a task where one clear profession is uniquely prototypical).

The classroom whiteboard erasing scene is concrete, imageable, and has a clear prototype (teacher), but the janitor is too plausible for implausible_hard and the current plausible_hard and implausible_hard choices result in a collapsed plausibility gradient. Replacing the mid- and low-plausibility agents can yield a clean four-level gradient.

The scene 'feeding a baby with a bottle in a nursery' is conceptually strong and supports a clear prototype and plausible/implausible contrasts, but the chosen agents cause both a plausibility misplacement (lactation consultant) and serious visual-identifiability problems (mother and lactation consultant); better-chosen, more visually distinct professional roles would fix it.

The robbery-in-a-convenience-store scene with fist-fighting is coherent, has a strong prototypical agent, and can support all four plausibility levels with better-chosen agents. The fishing-at-a-lakeside scene with a rod and trout is concrete, imageable, and has a strong prototype (fisherman), with good semantic separation across all four conditions. The only serious problem is the visual identifiability of the pianist, not the underlying scene or gradient structure.

Semantically, the kitchen-counter mug repair scene is suitable and can support a strong plausibility gradient with appropriate agents; the current top two agents are swapped in strength. The main challenge is visual: the prototypical domestic role (mother) is not visually identifiable as a profession/social role on a plain background, so the agent set must be revised to balance thematic fit with visual recognizability.

The kitchen-cheese-grating event is well-formed, has a clear cooking prototype, and is easy to depict. The main issues are the over-plausibility and poor visual identifiability of the 'home cook' as plausible_hard; substituting a more clearly secondary yet still kitchen-adjacent role would yield a better gradient.

The ironing-a-dress scene with a steam iron and ironing board is concrete, instrument-appropriate, and easily photographed, with clear potential prototypes in housekeeping and garment-care domains. While the knitting-in-an-armchair scenario is vivid and has a clear stereotypical agent, it functions as a generic leisure activity rather than a profession-specific action, so related roles tend to be plausible rather than truly implausible_hard. The chapel candle-lighting scene is concrete and imageable with an appropriate instrument and a clear religious prototype, but the chosen plausible_easy role is not visually identifiable and the distinction between the two plausible conditions is weak; these issues can be resolved by substituting more standard, visually distinct roles.

The laboratory–microscope scene is concrete, imageable, and has a strong prototype (a lab scientist/biologist). The current implausible_hard agent is too plausible, but alternative agents from adjacent medical domains could fix the gradient without changing the verb, instrument, or location.

The construction-site measuring scene is semantically strong and supports a clear four-level gradient, but two of the agents lack distinctive visual identities, so the experimental issue lies in agent choice rather than in the scene or action.

The kitchen–chocolate–hair-dryer scene is coherent and has a clear culinary prototype, but the chosen agents compress the top (chef vs baker) and bottom (cosmetologist vs librarian) of the gradient, and the librarian fails visual identifiability. Opening a wooden crate with a crowbar in a warehouse is a concrete, easily imaged action with a strong prototype in cargo workers. The basic scene (painting a backyard fence with a brush) is well-formed and has a clear prototypical agent, but because backyard fence-painting is a common chore for many adults, the chosen homeowner, carpenter, and librarian are all perceived as quite plausible and the visual identifiability of homeowner is poor. The scene ‘paying a restaurant bill with a credit card at the dining table’ has a clear prototype (customer) and is easy to picture, but paying a restaurant bill is a ubiquitous everyday activity for virtually all adults, independent of profession. The action and setting are clear and imageable with a strong prototype (chef), but the chosen implausible_hard agent is not sufficiently implausible given how ordinary it is for a farmer to cook; adjusting that agent should yield a robust plausibility gradient.

The event 'pinching a child's arm with fingers in a classroom' is concrete and photographable, and a school-based adult is a coherent high-fit agent, but the chosen agents do not yield a clean plausibility gradient and two of them lack distinctive visual identities. With more carefully selected and visually distinctive roles, the same scene could support the intended four-level gradient.

The gardening scene is conceptually strong and imageable with a clear core profession, but the current choice and placement of agents (especially the landscaper and librarian, and the visually weak homeowner role) prevent a clean plausibility gradient and robust visual discrimination.

The coffee-with-French-press-in-kitchen scene is concrete, imageable, and has a clear coffee-specialist prototype (barista). The main issue is that the chosen implausible_hard agent lacks the required domain overlap, but alternative agents exist that would support a proper plausibility gradient.

The raking-leaves-on-a-front-lawn scene with a metal rake is concrete, imageable, and has a clear prototype (a landscaper or similar groundskeeper), but the gardener is far too plausible for implausible_hard and the homeowner is visually unidentifiable; with better-chosen agents the gradient can be implemented cleanly.

Although the instrument and setting are coherent and imageable, the action of merely seeing a shooting star is too generic to generate clear implausibility based on professional roles, and at least one profession (meteorologist) is visually unidentifiable, so the scene does not support the required four-level plausibility gradient.

The ice-cream-scooping-in-an-ice-cream-shop scene is concrete, has an obvious prototype role, and uses an appropriate instrument. The sewing-workshop scene is concrete, has an appropriate instrument, and can in principle support all four plausibility levels, but the current agents collapse the top two levels and fail to provide a truly borderline related-but-wrong professional.

The barbershop beard-shaving scene is concrete, prototypical, and easy to depict, with a strong plausible_easy agent and a solid implausible_hard option. The kitchen buttering scene is well-formed and has an obvious prototypical agent; the only breakdown is that the current implausible_hard agent does not meet the multi-dimensional overlap requirement and behaves like a clear mismatch. Replacing that agent with a more closely related but contextually inappropriate food professional would restore a clean plausibility gradient.

The kitchen–soup–wooden-spoon scene is concrete, instrument-appropriate, and has a clear prototype (chef), but the current selection and placement of agents do not produce a clean plausibility gradient and one agent ('home cook') lacks a distinct visual identity. With better-chosen professional roles, the same scene could work well.

The scene itself is simple, physically coherent, and imageable, with an appropriate instrument for 'swat'. Sweeping a wooden hallway floor with a broom is a clear, easily photographed action with a strong prototypical agent (janitor) and room for systematically varying plausibility via agent choice.

The scene of throwing a baseball on a baseball diamond with different sports and non-sports professions provides a clear prototypical agent and supports distinct plausibility levels without relying on subtle reasoning.

The NICU newborn-touching scene is concrete, imageable, and has strong medical prototypes, but the nurse and pediatrician have been assigned to overly low plausibility levels; replacing or reassigning agents can yield a clean four-level gradient.

The towing-on-highway scene is concrete, uses an appropriate instrument, and has a clear professional prototype. It naturally supports a graded plausibility structure with related roadside and heavy-equipment professions contrasted against an unrelated artistic profession.

The domestic vacuuming scene itself is coherent, concrete, and has an obvious cleaning prototype, but the chosen non-prototypical agents are too plausible and one role (homeowner) lacks a visual identity. The car-washing-in-driveway scene is concrete, has an appropriate instrument, and can in principle support a full plausibility gradient, but the current agents (especially homeowner) and their assignments do not yield a clear gradient and introduce identifiability issues.

The basic action of watering tomato plants with a watering can in a backyard is clear, imageable, and has obvious prototypical agents, but the chosen agents do not optimally realize the plausibility gradient and one role (homeowner) lacks a distinct visual identity.

The post-office weighing scene is concrete and easily photographed, with a strong core professional (postal worker) and clear room for graded plausibility. However, using 'customer' as an agent fails the visual identifiability requirement, so agent substitutions are needed for experimental use.

The basic backyard-digging-with-a-shovel scene is well-formed and supports a full plausibility gradient, but the current selection misplaces the homeowner and construction worker, and uses a visually unidentifiable ‘homeowner’ role.

The main problem is the choice of line cook for implausible_hard; with a more suitable overlapping-but-wrong profession, the gradient could be well realized.

The event itself is concrete and easily photographed, and a clear security/banking prototype exists for the action. The current misplacement of the locksmith affects the gradient, but alternative, thematically and visually suitable agents are available within this scene to restore a proper plausibility hierarchy.

Painting a wooden backyard fence with a paintbrush is a clear, photographable scene with a strong prototype (house painter) and an appropriate instrument. The main problems are that the chosen implausible_hard agent is too plausible and the plausible_hard agent lacks a visually identifiable role; both can be remedied by substituting better-chosen agents while keeping the scene unchanged.
The scene uses an appropriate instrument, has a clear core profession, is easily depicted in a single image, and supports a clean plausibility gradient with well-separated agents.

Shooting a basketball on a court with the hands is a well-defined, easily photographed action with a clear prototypical agent and ample room to vary related and unrelated professions for gradient construction.

The kitchen-soup-wooden-spoon scene is concrete, easily photographed, and has a clear prototypical agent (chef). The current agents mostly support a plausible-to-implausible gradient, but the pharmacist as implausible_hard is somewhat abstract in its overlap with the chef, and a hospitality-role replacement would strengthen the gradient.

The hospital-room/stethoscope scene is coherent and has a clear medical prototype, and photos would be straightforward to generate. The current agent mapping fails to respect the plausibility gradient, especially by under-rating the doctor and over-penalizing the paramedic, but these are correctable by choosing and reassigning appropriate medical and non-medical roles.

The hospital-bed-cleaning scene is concrete, uses a suitable instrument, and can support the full plausibility gradient. While ‘writing a letter with a pen at a wooden desk’ is a coherent, imageable event with a reasonable prototype (secretary), it is so generic that almost any educated professional can plausibly occupy the role, making it nearly impossible to construct a semantically related-but-wrong implausible_hard agent. The action, instrument, and location are coherent and easily photographed; there is a strong prototypical agent and clear room for a graded plausibility continuum with visually distinct, identifiable roles.

While the toothbrush/teeth/bathroom configuration is coherent and easy to visualize, tooth-brushing in a bathroom is generic self-care rather than a profession-specific action, so almost any human role fits plausibly. A redesigned scene that situates tooth-related actions in a professional setting (e.g., dental clinic, patient in a chair) would better support the intended gradient.

The backyard birdhouse-building scene is concrete, imageable, and uses an appropriate instrument, with a decent prototype in the carpenter. However, the chosen middle agents (handyman and especially bricklayer) are too plausible for their assigned levels, collapsing the gradient; with alternative agents that create a clearer stepwise drop in role appropriateness, the scene could function well.

The industrial-yard blowtorch scene is concrete and photographable, with a strong prototypical association between welders and blowtorches and a clear unrelated role (ballet dancer). The main issue is misassignment of firefighter and carpenter along the plausibility gradient, not the underlying scene design or instrument choice.

The action 'burying a time capsule with a shovel in the schoolyard' is coherent, physically appropriate, and imageable, and there are clear professional roles that can serve as strong prototypes and graded foils. Catching a baseball with a glove on a baseball diamond is a concrete, easily imageable scene with a strong prototype (catcher). The selected agents cover clear yes, hesitant yes, hesitant no, and clear no, and the action-instrument pairing is appropriate.

The cooking-a-steak-in-a-kitchen scene is clear, has an obvious prototype (chef), and is easily photographable; the main issue is that the firefighter does not provide the required nuanced implausible_hard overlap and should be replaced by a more food-adjacent but role-mismatched profession.

Cutting a loaf of bread with a knife on a kitchen counter is a concrete, easily photographable scene with a clear culinary prototype and room for semantically related but wrong agents. The chosen agents create a coherent plausibility gradient and are visually distinctive and identifiable.
